chunk_findings.detail:
The change drops the stash digest from `git_state`, on the stated grounds that any reviewer stash activity "still shows in the working tree and index." That claim only holds for `git stash apply`/`git stash push`/`git stash pop` when they actually mutate the tree. It does not hold for operations that consume the shared stash list *without* touching HEAD, the index, or the working tree — which is exactly the harm B5ce30dd94d added the digest for ("a reviewer that runs `git stash apply|pop` ... consumes another lane's work").

Concrete inputs where the guard is now blind:

- Gate command `git stash drop stash@{0}` (or `git stash clear`, `git stash store`, `git stash branch`): the stash entry is removed but `rev-parse HEAD`, the index digest, `status --porcelain`, and `diff HEAD` are all byte-identical before and after, so `git_state(...) == git_state(...)` and the review is reported clean. The old code detected this via the `stash` digest; now another worktree's stashed work is destroyed silently and the gate says nothing.
- Gate command `git stash pop && git checkout -- .` (a plausible "get changes, then clean up" reviewer flow): pop consumes the shared stash entry and mutates the tree only transiently; the tree/index are restored before the post-snapshot, so again the only observable change is the stash list, and it is no longer observed.

The false-positive problem this removal is meant to solve (a sibling worktree mutating the shared `refs/stash` mid-review) is real, but the fix removes the protection instead of scoping or tolerating it; the residual uncovered case should at minimum be called out as accepted risk rather than asserted away in the docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:208 (the `parts` dict — removed `"stash": ("stash", "list", "--format=%H %gs")`)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard now samples the git state of `tree`, the repo being reviewed. That isolates per-worktree state (HEAD, index, `git status`), but it does not isolate state that git keeps in the repository's *common* dir and therefore shares across every linked worktree of that repository — most notably `refs/stash` / the stash reflog. The bug this change is fixing says explicitly that "stash list is shared", which is only observable if `git_state` records the stash list (otherwise a stash in a sibling lane could never have tripped the guard). Given that, the failure scenario is unchanged for the case the bug title names: ddflow runs in worktree A of repo R and reviews worktree B of the same R; while the reviewer runs, another lane executes `git stash` in worktree C (or A) of R. `git -C <B> stash list` still returns the new entry, so `git_state_change(before, after)` is non-empty and the review is again rejected with "the reviewer tool changed git state" — the exact false positive B708761957b reports. The change only fixes the cross-repository case (ddflow's checkout is a different clone, e.g. the tests' real checkout vs. the temp repo fixture); for the sibling-worktree case stated in the bug and in the docstring ("a sibling lane commits (B708761957b)"), commits are now filtered out because HEAD/status are per-worktree, but stashes are not. A fix that actually isolates the reviewed tree would have to drop repo-shared state (the stash reflog) from the comparison, or scope the guard to per-worktree state only, rather than merely changing which path `git_state` is pointed at.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:758 (`_tool_moved` / `state_before = git_state(tree or os.getcwd())`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the `"stash"` entry (`("stash", "list", "--format=%H %gs")`) from the watched `parts`, leaving only HEAD/index/worktree. That is justified for a sibling lane's `git stash`, but it also silently drops detection of stash-list operations that leave the tree untouched, so a reviewer can now destroy shared (other-lane) stash entries and still be reported as clean. Concrete case: the reviewed repo has an existing stash from another lane; the reviewer command runs `git stash drop stash@{0}` (or `git stash clear`, or `git stash store <commit>`). `git status --porcelain=v2`/`git diff HEAD` are unchanged and `rev-parse HEAD` is unchanged, so the before and after dicts are equal and `_run_with_git_guard` returns the gate as available — whereas before this change the differing `stash list` made it `unavailable`. The same blind spot exists for `git stash push --keep-index` when only staged work is present: the index and working tree are kept, the stash list grows, and the guard no longer notices. This narrows the protection that bug B5ce30dd94d deliberately introduced ("consumes another lane's work"), and the error string at line ~287 still tells the operator to "check the tree and `git stash list` before going on", i.e. the code still assumes a guarantee it no longer enforces.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:200 (`git_state` parts dict — removal of `"stash"`)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard was retargeted to `tree`, but the reviewer process is still launched in the process cwd — the old comment it replaced ("its cwd is this process's") is still true, since `_RUNNER.start(...)` is not given `cwd=tree`. That makes the check blind in exactly the case the change is meant to handle. Concrete input: `rev.kind == "command"`, `tree=/tmp/reviewed` (the reviewed checkout, a different directory from the process cwd), process cwd `[REDACTED:path]`, reviewer command `git commit --allow-empty -m x`. Before this diff, `state_before = git_state(os.getcwd())` was snapshotted in the directory the tool actually runs in, so the after-state differed and the run was rejected with "the reviewer tool changed git state". After this diff, `_tool_moved(state_before, tree)` compares `git_state(/tmp/reviewed)` before/after — a repo the subprocess never ran in and did not touch — so it returns `""`, the completion is accepted, and the mutation to `[REDACTED:path]` (the directory the reviewer *does* operate in, by relative paths) goes unreported. The guard added by B5ce30dd94d is therefore effectively vacuous whenever `tree != os.getcwd()`; to keep it meaningful, the subprocess needs to be started with `cwd=tree` (or the before/after comparison must watch the directory the tool is actually launched in as well).

chunk_findings.detail: This is prior finding #1, and I do not think it is refuted. The stated probe (`test_git_state_ignores_the_shared_stash_list`) only exercises the *false-positive* side of the bug — that a sibling lane's `git stash` no longer moves the watched state — and the new docstring only claims cover for `git stash apply|pop` and `stash push`. Neither addresses the false-negative that B5ce30dd94d added the stash digest to catch: operations that mutate the *shared* stash ref while leaving HEAD, the index and the working tree untouched. Concrete input: review a repo with a clean tree while a sibling lane has an entry at `stash@{0}`; the reviewer command runs `git stash drop` (or `git stash clear`). After the change, `git_state` samples only head/ref/status/diff, so `before == after` for every remaining part and `_tool_moved` reports no movement — the gate returns a clean, trustworthy review even though the sibling lane's stashed work has been destroyed. The same applies to `git stash pop` in the case where the stash's content already matches the working tree (the entry is consumed with no tree diff) and to `git stash push --keep-index` with only staged changes (entry created, tree/index unchanged). The author's note ("Stash drop/clear leaves tree untouched, undetected now. Accepted trade-off required by the bug") is not a probe of this behavior; it explicitly concedes it. Since the shared stash list cannot be watched without reintroducing the false positive, this is at minimum a real, surviving loss of coverage relative to the state before this change, and it is not covered by any regression test added here.

data.probe: Not a defect: a deliberate, now test-pinned trade-off (test_known_gap_a_stash_drop_alone_is_not_seen). The shared stash list cannot be watched without the sibling-stash false positive this bug reports; drop/clear alone is the residual gap, apply/pop/push are still caught.

chunk_findings.detail: The probe that refuted the earlier report says "stash apply/pop/push all alter the tree/index and are still caught (tests)". That is only true while the tree is still altered *at snapshot time*. With the `"stash"` entry deleted, the guard compares only HEAD/index/worktree; a reviewer that consumes a (shared, repo-global) stash entry and then puts the worktree back cannot be distinguished from a clean review. Concrete input: the reviewed worktree is clean at snapshot; another lane's work is sitting in the shared stash list; the reviewer command is `git stash pop && pytest -q; git reset --hard HEAD`. `git stash pop` deletes the top stash entry (the sibling lane's only copy, since the stash list is repo-global), `git reset --hard HEAD` restores index and worktree to HEAD, so `head`/`index`/`status`/`diff` digests all equal the pre-review snapshot and the gate is reported as a clean review — even though a sibling lane's stashed work was destroyed. `git stash drop`/`clear` reach the same end state without the intermediate dirtiness. The fix's own docstring/message now claims the reviewer's stash activity "still shows in the working tree and index", which is exactly what this sequence defeats; the correct mitigation would be to keep detecting stash-list mutation and instead exclude only the sibling-lane false positive (e.g. snapshot the stash list per worktree/lane, or compare stash entries against the pre-review set), rather than dropping the part entirely and losing a class of data-destroying reviewer behaviour.
